_comment: The three repeal-and-savings provisions the transition stream turns on, one per code family. THESE ARE NOT QUOTATIONS AND DO NOT CLAIM TO BE: this repository holds no bare-act corpus (the only other statute resource, ipc_bns_map.jsonl, carries section numbers and marginal notes and nothing else), so each row records the provision's OPERATIVE EFFECT as the pipeline's own decision table already states it, and text_kind says so on every row. `derived_from` names where the statement comes from - src/tuned/data/statutes.py's module docstring, which is the audited source of the two rules the whole pipeline applies, and which cross_code_review and governing_family implement. There is deliberately NO verified_by field here: an audit stamp this file wrote about itself would be theatre, and the honest reading is that these three blocks are transcriptions of a rule the build already depends on rather than independent readings of the bare Act. OPERATOR QUEUE: when a bare-act corpus lands (P7), replace `effect` with the section text, add verified_by, and flip text_kind to "verbatim" - transition.py reads the field and will carry whichever is there.

title: Repeal and savings
effect: Sub-section (2) preserves the effect of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897. The repeal of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 does not affect any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under it, nor any penalty or punishment incurred in respect of an offence committed against it, and any investigation, legal proceeding or remedy in respect of such a liability or penalty may be instituted, continued or enforced, and any such penalty imposed, as if that Code had not been repealed. An offence committed before the appointed day is therefore charged and punished under the Indian Penal Code however long afterwards the matter is taken up; the passage of time never converts it into an offence under this Sanhita.
derived_from: src/tuned/data/statutes.py module docstring and governing_family(): the substantive rule the pipeline applies

title: Repeal and savings
effect: Sub-section (2)(a): an appeal, application, trial, inquiry or investigation pending immediately before the commencement of this Sanhita is disposed of, continued, held or made under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 as it stood before the commencement. Anything instituted on or after the appointed day is conducted under this Sanhita instead - even where the offence to which it relates was committed before that day, because what this provision turns on is whether the proceeding was already pending, not when the conduct occurred.
derived_from: src/tuned/data/statutes.py module docstring and governing_family(): the procedural rule the pipeline applies

title: Repeal and savings
effect: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam repeals the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and saves proceedings pending immediately before the commencement on the same footing as the procedural savings above: evidence in such a proceeding continues to be received under the Indian Evidence Act as it stood, while a proceeding begun on or after the appointed day receives evidence under this Adhiniyam.
